Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches (checked out, one prior commit 9f46912 already landed — do NOT touch overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx, that step is done). This is SFCC-91 Step 2 of 4. Do not stage, do not commit — the loop will handle that after review.

TASK: create a new atom, `ZimmColourSwatch`, under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/`. Mirror the four-file pattern at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode/` (read it first — file structure, JSDoc density, comment tone, house formatting) and `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductMeta/` if useful for a second reference point.

FILES TO CREATE — exactly these four, plus one edit to a fifth file:
1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` (the recipe)
2. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` (the component)
3. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.stories.tsx`
4. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/index.test.tsx`
5. Edit `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — add one import + one key for the new recipe, alongside the existing ui-kits imports (e.g. next to `ZimmProductStyleCode`). Do not touch anything else in that file.

Do NOT touch: overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx, overrides/app/components/swatch-group/ (doesn't exist, don't create it), overrides/app/components/image-gallery/, translations/*.json, overrides/app/theme/foundation/ (Tier 1, absolute — if you think you need a new token, STOP and report back instead of adding one).

## Why this ordering matters (read before writing anything)

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` walks `overrides/app/components/**` for `*.css.ts` files, and for any recipe declaring a `parts:` array, asserts its sibling `index.tsx` exists. If you create the `.css.ts` file and run `npm run test` before the `index.tsx` exists, that specific test will fail. It's fine to author them in any order as long as both exist by the time you run the full verification pass at the end — just don't be alarmed by an interim failure if you check tests mid-way.

## The recipe — `zimmColourSwatch.css.ts`

Export name: `ZimmColourSwatch` (exact casing matters — a key literally named `Swatch` or `SwatchGroup` would deep-merge with base SFCC's own `SwatchGroup` theme recipe via `extendTheme`'s deep-merge behavior, and fail `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard, which only permits `Button`/`Header`/`ListMenu` to intentionally merge with a base recipe).

`parts: ['swatch', 'image']` — `swatch` is the outer clickable box (geometry, background, border, focus ring); `image` is the element carrying the dynamic background-image fill.

I pulled the exact design values directly from Figma (not estimated from metadata) for the three states — Unselected (node 40000307:13826), Selected (40000307:13831), Focus (40002689:3839), all under `size=Large/Rectangle`. Use EXACTLY these, mapped to EXISTING zimm tokens (all confirmed to exist, do not invent anything):

- **Container size:** width 48px → `var(--zimm-scale-1200)`. Height 72px has no direct token (gap in the scale between 64px and 140px) — express it as `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` on the 48px width instead of a raw height value. This is confirmed correct, not a guess: the Figma node for the Selected state carries an explicit dev annotation reading "Image aspect ratio - 2:3" — trust that annotation over the incidentally-different `aspect-[1000/1300]` ratio Figma's raw code-gen attached to the inner sample product photo (that ratio just reflects whatever placeholder image happened to be pasted into that particular frame instance, not a design decision).
- **Background, ALL THREE states identical:** `#f6f4f1`, which is `ivory[200]` in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts`, which is `background['02']` — use `var(--zimm-color-background-02)`.
- **Unselected state:** background only, no border, no outline.
- **Selected state:** same background, PLUS a BOTTOM-ONLY border (not a full box border — the raw Figma export is unambiguous: Tailwind's `border-b` utility, not `border`). Colour is `#191919`, which is `grey[900]`, which is `overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s `border.focus` (NOT `border.default` or `border.secondary` — I checked, those are both light greys and never appear in this design at all; only `.focus` resolves to `#191919`). Use `var(--zimm-border-width-default)` (1px) `solid` `var(--zimm-color-border-focus)`, applied as `borderBottom` — e.g. `borderBottomWidth: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)', borderBottomStyle: 'solid', borderBottomColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)'`.
- **Focus state:** Figma implements this as the Selected-state baseline (same background, same bottom border) PLUS a separate ring drawn just outside the box, at slightly asymmetric per-side offsets (-2px/-2.13px/-3px/-2px) using the same #191919 colour. Do NOT replicate Figma's asymmetric per-side implementation literally — there is an existing codebase precedent for exactly this kind of focus ring, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmNavItem/zimmNavItem.css.ts` (read it), which uses a uniform CSS `outline: var(--zimm-focus-ring)` + `outlineOffset: var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` inside a `_focusVisible` pseudo-selector block. Mirror that exact pattern here — `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` already composites 1px solid `border.focus` (i.e. the same #191919), and `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` is 2px, matching three of Figma's four sides (the 2.13px/3px asymmetry is judged to be that specific frame instance's export noise, not a deliberate design decision — there is no other precedent anywhere in this codebase for a non-uniform ring). Apply this via `_focusVisible` so it triggers on real keyboard focus, independent of the `selected` variant prop (a component can be focused without being selected, and selected without being focused).

`baseStyle` should be a function of `{selected}: {selected?: boolean}` (safe to do — `recipeGuards.test.ts` always invokes baseStyle with an object across all its test combinations and walks both the `selected: true` and `selected: false` branches). The `_focusVisible` outline block applies regardless of `selected` — it's a separate concern from the border-bottom.

Every colour/space/border value must be a `var(--zimm-*)` reference — no bare hex, no bare px/rem literal, no bare Chakra token key. Run a self-check with `grep -nE "#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}|[0-9]+px|[0-9.]+rem|[0-9.]+em" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/zimmColourSwatch.css.ts` before you're done — it should return nothing.

## The component — `index.tsx`

Props type (declare at top of file, JSDoc each field per this codebase's convention):
```ts
type ZimmColourSwatchProps = {
  name: string;        // colour display name, used as aria-label
  imageUrl: string;    // already resolved by the caller (this component does no SFCC-shape resolution)
  href?: string;
  isSelected: boolean;
  isFocusable: boolean;
};
```

- `useMultiStyleConfig('ZimmColourSwatch', { selected: isSelected })`, called above any early return (there shouldn't be one here — this component always renders something, unlike zimmProductStyleCode which can return null).
- Module scope (not inside the component body): `const ColourSwatchLink = chakra(RouteLink)`, where `RouteLink` is `Link` imported from `react-router-dom` — the exact same import base SFCC's own `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group/swatch.jsx:16` uses for its own `RouteLink`. This is what actually delivers AC 4 (URL updates without a full page reload) — a router `Link` pushes history, it doesn't navigate the document. There is no `overrides/.../link` override to reuse instead — confirmed none exists.
- When `href` is present: render `<ColourSwatchLink to={href} __css={styles.swatch} role="radio" aria-checked={isSelected} aria-label={name} tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1} data-testid="colour-swatch">`.
- When `href` is absent: render a plain `<chakra.span __css={styles.swatch} role="radio" aria-checked={isSelected} aria-label={name} tabIndex={isFocusable ? 0 : -1} data-testid="colour-swatch">` instead — no anchor element at all. This matters for Storybook/Vitest (no router needed for this branch) and for the controlled quick-view-modal path where SFCC's own `useVariationAttributes` returns `href: null`.
- Inside either wrapper, one child: `<chakra.span __css={{ ...styles.image, backgroundImage: \`url(${imageUrl})\` }} />`. The dynamic URL genuinely cannot live in the static recipe file, so this one dynamic `__css` spread is the correct, deliberate exception — it's the same shape already used at `overrides/app/components/footer/footerNavColumn/index.tsx:44` and `:62`, so it's an established pattern in this codebase, not a new one.
- **Deliberately do NOT add** base SFCC's `backgroundColor={name.toLowerCase()}` behavior (visible in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-view/index.jsx` if you want to see it, or in our own extracted `renderDefaultVariationAttribute` in product-view/index.tsx). Write a code comment at the point where a reader might expect it, explaining: it uses the colour's display name as a raw CSS colour keyword ("Ivory" resolves as a real CSS colour, "Bay Blue" does not) — unauditable by `audit:tokens` and against this codebase's no-raw-design-values rule; it exists in base to tint behind a *missing* product image, and this component is only ever rendered for colour variations that DO have a populated image (the caller filters unpopulated ones out before rendering this component at all); and `background-size: cover` on the image would hide the tint behind the photo anyway even if it were present. This is a deliberate, permanent divergence from base, not an oversight — say so plainly in the comment so a future reader doesn't "fix" it back in.
- No `sx` prop anywhere, no data-fetching hook of any kind (this is a pure presentational leaf — SFCC data resolution happens at the page level, not built yet, that's Step 4).

## The story — `index.stories.tsx`

`title: 'Commerce/ZimmColourSwatch'`. Because this component may render a react-router `Link`, and `.storybook/preview.tsx` supplies Chakra + Intl context globally but NOT a router (confirmed — `.storybook/` is Tier 1, so you cannot add a global router decorator there even if you wanted to), you must add a **local decorator** in this story file wrapping renders in `MemoryRouter` from `react-router-dom`.

Named exports: `Default` (with an `href`, unselected, focusable), `Selected` (isSelected=true), `WithoutLink` (no `href`, to exercise the `chakra.span` branch). Use a real-looking placeholder image URL for `imageUrl` (any working https URL is fine — doesn't need to resolve to a real product).

## The test — `index.test.tsx`

Wrap all renders in `MemoryRouter` (same reason as the story). Assert only this atom's own contract — nothing about how a parent would compose it:
1. `href` present → the rendered element (`getByRole('radio')`) is an anchor with that exact `href` attribute.
2. `href` absent → `getByRole('radio')` exists but is NOT an anchor element (check `tagName`, should not be `'A'`).
3. `isSelected={true}` → `aria-checked="true"`; `isSelected={false}` → `aria-checked="false"`.
4. `isFocusable={true}` → `tabIndex` is `0`; `isFocusable={false}` → `tabIndex` is `-1`.
5. The `imageUrl` you pass appears in the rendered element's inline `background-image` style (check via the DOM, e.g. `element.style.backgroundImage` on the inner image span, or however Chakra's `__css` resolves it in the test environment — verify this actually works before finalizing, don't assume).
6. **Regression guard, exact wording matters:** render with `name="Bay Blue"` and assert the rendered swatch box element's `style.backgroundColor === ''` (empty string, meaning nothing was set) — this is the test that keeps the deliberate no-backgroundColor divergence from silently regressing if someone "fixes" it back in later.

No `ZimmIcon` is used anywhere in this component, so you do not need the known ZimmIcon-throws-under-Vitest mock.

## Verification — run these yourself, report exact output, do not just say "passed"

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Baselines already established on this branch (compare counts/identity, not exit codes — both lint and audit:tokens exit 1 at a HEALTHY baseline):
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — must be 0 errors.
- `npm run test` — was 26 files / 408 tests before Step 1's commit; Step 1 added no test file. You are adding exactly one new test file, so expect 27 files and MORE than 408 tests (report the exact new numbers).
- `npm run lint` — was 20 problems (4 errors, 16 warnings), the 4 errors pre-existing in `overrides/app/routes.tsx:23,24` and `overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts:116,335` — NOT your files. Your new files should add ZERO new errors; report if you see any and where.
- `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` — was exactly 4 unacknowledged / 22 acknowledged before your change. Your new recipe file must add ZERO new unacknowledged findings (it's fine, expected even, for the audit's "acknowledged" count to grow if you legitimately need to write an `audit-allow:` comment somewhere unusual, but you shouldn't need one at all if you use only `var(--zimm-*)` tokens throughout).

Also run and report:
```
grep -c "ZimmColourSwatch" overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
```
Must return exactly 2 (one import line, one key in the exported object).

```
npm run test 2>&1 | grep -i "zimmColourSwatch\|recipeParts"
```
Confirm `recipeParts.test.ts` actually collected and passed a case for this new recipe (proves it was tested, not silently skipped because of a naming mismatch between the recipe file and what the test scans for).

**Mutation check — do this for real, don't just assert it would work.** Temporarily edit your own test file to hardcode `aria-checked` as a constant `"true"` string in the component regardless of the `isSelected` prop (i.e. deliberately break the selected-state logic), re-run just that one test, confirm it actually FAILS, then revert the component back to the real logic and confirm the test passes again. Report both the failing-run output and the passing-run output — a check that has never been observed to fail does not count as verified per this project's standard.

Report back: full output of every command above, confirmation that all 4 files were created and the theme index was edited with exactly a 2-line change, and the mutation check's before/after output.

9	 * is exactly `spacing['2xs']`.

11	 * Open with the designer (see the PR body): the DS models this as two nodes while both
12	 * composed page designs show a single concatenated string, "Style Code: 7300JS261". A flex
13	 * row of two nodes renders identically to the concatenation, so this satisfies both until the
14	 * question is settled.

17	 * `styleProps` *after* `__css` (`assignAfter({}, __css, finalBaseStyle,
18	 * filterUndefined(styleProps), sx)`, dist/index.js lines 204-213), and `assignAfter` re-inserts a
19	 * duplicate key — so a `textStyle=` on the JSX would displace this one. `root` is the right part:
20	 * `label` and `value` inherit the type from it, so it is declared once, not on each of the two.

32	      // copy above it. Our `--zimm-color-text-secondary` resolves to grey[600] = #666666, an exact

2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { useIntl } from 'react-intl';
4	
5	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductStyleCode';
6	
7	/*
8	 * The label is UI copy, so it is a translatable message rather than a literal. `defaultMessage`
9	 * carries the English inline, which is what makes this work with no `translations/` entry: that
10	 * directory is Tier 2 (owner Integration/SI Partner) and is populated by the extraction step, so
11	 * a component cannot add to it. Until extraction runs, every locale renders `defaultMessage`;
12	 * once it does, the eleven locales pick up their own string with no change here.
13	 *
14	 * The id follows the base template's namespace for PDP labels — `product_view.label.quantity`
15	 * and `product_view.label.variant_type` are its siblings — so a translator finds it with the
16	 * rest of the PDP copy.
17	 */
18	const LABEL_MESSAGE = {
19	  id: 'product_view.label.style_code',
20	  defaultMessage: 'Style Code:',
21	};
22	
23	type ZimmProductStyleCodeProps = {
24	  /**
25	   * The master product's style number. This is the style code shown to shoppers, which is not
26	   * the same value as the variant `product.id`.
27	   */
28	  value?: string;
29	};
30	
31	/**
32	 * Atom — the "Style Code: 7300JS261" line. Renders nothing when no style code is available.
33	 *
34	 * The label comes from `react-intl`, not from CMS microcopy and not from a literal. A `uiCopy`
35	 * lookup is the wrong tool here — `useContentful.ts` requests entries with no `locale`
36	 * parameter, so it would serve the space default to all eight storefronts regardless of site —
37	 * but a bare literal is not the remedy for that, it just ships English to all eleven locales
38	 * instead. `formatMessage` is the base template's own mechanism and is per-locale by
39	 * construction.
40	 *
41	 * components.md exempts `useIntl` from the container/presentational rule: it reads a Provider
42	 * mounted above the route tree, so calling it from a leaf creates none of the per-page fetch
43	 * problems that rule exists to prevent. It does *throw* without an `IntlProvider` — the app
44	 * mounts one in the base `_app`, `.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts one for stories, and
45	 * `index.test.tsx` wraps its renders for the same reason.
46	 */
47	export const ZimmProductStyleCode = ({ value }: ZimmProductStyleCodeProps) => {
48	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_STYLE_CODE_RECIPE, {});
49	  // `intl.formatMessage`, not a destructured `{ formatMessage }`: destructuring a method off
50	  // `useIntl()` trips `@typescript-eslint/unbound-method`, which `staticProductHeader.tsx` has to
51	  // suppress inline. `product-view/index.tsx` uses this form throughout and needs no suppression.
52	  const intl = useIntl();
53	  // Both hooks sit above the guard: an early return before either makes that call conditional,
54	  // which `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` reports as an error. Same ordering as the sibling atoms.
55	  if (!value) return null;
56	
57	  return (
58	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-style-code">
59	      <chakra.span __css={styles.label}>{intl.formatMessage(LABEL_MESSAGE)}</chakra.span>
60	      {/*
61	        A real space so `textContent` — what a screen reader reads out and what a shopper
62	        copies — is "Style Code: 8637DS241", matching both composed page designs. It adds no
63	        visual width: a whitespace-only anonymous flex item is not rendered (CSS Flexbox §4),
64	        so the 4px `gap` in the recipe remains the only spacing.
65	      */}{' '}
66	      <chakra.span __css={styles.value}>{value}</chakra.span>
67	    </chakra.div>
68	  );
69	};

41	      flexDirection: 'column',

/**
 * Recipe for the PDP meta block — the model line and the style code, which the design places
 * at the bottom of the info column below the accordions.
 *
 * Multipart with a single `root` part rather than a bare `baseStyle`: `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts`
 * reconciles a declared `parts` array against what the sibling component actually reads off
 * `useMultiStyleConfig`, and a recipe with no `parts` key is skipped by that walk entirely.
 * Declaring the one part buys the reconciliation for the two-node shape this block will grow
 * into when the designer settles the label/value question raised in `zimmProductStyleCode.css.ts`.
 */

/**
 * DS: 28px between the drawers and the model line, and again between the model line and the
 * style code — identical on both breakpoints (pdp/product-content, desktop and mobile Default).
 * Figma: pdp/product-content, Desktop Default 40000307:14062 / Mobile Default 40000343:9727.
 *
 * A rem literal because no rem-valued 28px token exists to reference. `spacing.ts` brackets it
 * at `xl` (1.5rem/24px) and `2xl` (2rem/32px) with nothing between, and `--zimm-scale-700` — the
 * one alias that does hold 28px — is itself a raw px string in `zimmTokens.ts`, not a reference
 * to a named step the way its neighbours `--zimm-scale-600`/`-800` reference `spacing.xl`/`2xl`.
 * Substituting it would silently convert spacing that scales with the user's root font size into
 * fixed px, which is what overrideStyling.md's Units rule rules out for spacing (WCAG 1.4.4).
 *
 * `theme/components/listMenu.ts` (lines 17, 33, 65, 84) does use `var(--zimm-scale-700)` for its
 * own 28px, so the precedent in this repo is genuinely split — noted here so the next reader does
 * not read that file as evidence this one is wrong and "align" it into a px value. The Units rule
 * is what decides, and it points at rem for spacing. Pending a named 28px step from the UI
 * designer both should converge on; listMenu.ts is designer-owned Tier 2 and not this file's to
 * change. Do not swap for `xl` or `2xl`, both visibly wrong.
 */
const SPACE_META_ROW = '1.75rem'; // 28px at the default 16px root

export const ZimmProductMeta = {
  parts: ['root'],
  baseStyle: {
    // One const drives both hops because the design measures both at 28px. Written as a `gap`
    // plus a `paddingTop` on the same container — the pattern `footer.css.ts` (lines 41-42)
    // already uses with its own SPACE_SECTION — so the two cannot drift apart.
    root: {
      display: 'flex',
      flexDirection: 'column',
      alignItems: 'flex-start',
      gap: SPACE_META_ROW, // model line -> style code
      paddingTop: SPACE_META_ROW, // drawers -> model line
    },
  },
};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmProductModelInfo } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductModelInfo';
4	import { ZimmProductStyleCode } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductStyleCode';
5	import { isBlankRichText } from 'app/utils/richText';
6	
7	const ZIMM_PRODUCT_META_RECIPE = 'ZimmProductMeta';
8	
9	type ZimmProductMetaProps = {
10	  /**
11	   * Model copy from the product's `c_modelFit` attribute, rich text as authored in Business
12	   * Manager. Not populated on most catalogue products today.
13	   */
14	  modelInfo?: string;
15	  /**
16	   * The master product's style number. Named to match `PdpProductInfo`'s field rather than the
17	   * atom's `value`, so the page can hand this block the mapper's output directly.
18	   */
19	  styleCode?: string;
20	};
21	
22	/**
23	 * Molecule — the PDP meta block: the model line and the style code, in the order the design
24	 * places them beneath the accordions at the bottom of the info column.
25	 *
26	 * Both children already collapse on their own, so this exists for the spacing: the recipe owns
27	 * the 28px above the block and the 28px between its two rows.
28	 */
29	export const ZimmProductMeta = ({ modelInfo, styleCode }: ZimmProductMetaProps) => {
30	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_PRODUCT_META_RECIPE, {});
31	
32	  // LOAD-BEARING, not a redundant echo of the children's own guards. Every other collapse in
33	  // ui-kits/ happens in an atom and the parent spaces whatever rendered with `gap` alone —
34	  // zimmProductContent.css.ts documents exactly that, and it works because a `gap` applies only
35	  // between rendered items, so an all-null column measures zero. This recipe also carries a
36	  // `paddingTop`, and padding is unconditional: without this guard, a product with neither a
37	  // style code nor model copy would still push 28px of empty space below the accordions.
38	  //
39	  // The predicate deliberately repeats zimmProductModelInfo/index.tsx:19's
40	  // `isBlankRichText(modelInfo)`. DRY holds at the logic level — `isBlankRichText`
41	  // (app/utils/richText.tsx) is the one shared implementation — so what repeats is the
42	  // *decision* about what counts as absent. If the atom's guard ever changes, this must follow.
43	  if (isBlankRichText(modelInfo) && !styleCode) return null;
44	
45	  return (
46	    <chakra.div __css={styles.root} data-testid="product-meta">
47	      <ZimmProductModelInfo modelInfo={modelInfo} />
48	      <ZimmProductStyleCode value={styleCode} />
49	    </chakra.div>
50	  );
51	};

1	import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
2	
3	// Vertical leading around the label. Figma's footer-item allows equal space above and
4	// below the text and lets the item height follow the line count — 24px for one line,
5	// 38px for two (node 40000407:11736 > About Section > Links). Its text boxes are
6	// cap-height (8px one line, 22px two) where a browser line box is not, so the rule
7	// transfers rather than the numbers. The inner span reserves 1px for the underline
8	// indicator, so a line box measures 15px and two measure 29px; 4.5px each side yields
9	// 15+9=24 and 29+9=38 exactly. No 4.5px entry exists in spacing.ts — same provisional
10	// treatment as zimmButton.css.ts's BTN_PADDING_Y, pending UI-designer sign-off.
11	const NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y = '4.5px';
12	
13	const baseStyle = {
14	  // textStyle is expanded in place by Chakra's style engine; fontFamily below
15	  // deliberately overrides it — Figma Default/Navigation binds brand/font/family/body,
16	  // not the heading family textStyles.navigation carries.
17	  textStyle: 'navigation',
18	  fontFamily: 'var(--zimm-font-family-body)',
19	  display: 'inline-flex',
20	  // Figma h-[24px] is a FLOOR, not a fixed height — the design's own ABOUT column
21	  // wraps "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY" onto two lines. minHeight keeps the 24px
22	  // target while letting multi-line labels grow, so no caller needs to override it.
23	  minHeight: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 1.5rem (24px) — Figma: h-[24px]
24	  // Height comes from lineHeight + padding, not from centring inside minHeight.
25	  // Centring only distributes space a single line leaves over, so a wrapped label
26	  // overflowed the floor and lost its leading entirely — the second line of
27	  // "ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY" sat flush against the item above it.
28	  lineHeight: 'var(--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs)', // 0.875rem (14px)
29	  paddingBlock: NAV_ITEM_PAD_Y,
30	  justifyContent: 'center',
31	  alignItems: 'center',
32	  whiteSpace: 'normal',
33	  cursor: 'pointer',
34	  background: 'none',
35	  border: 'none',
36	  // paddingInline, not the `padding` shorthand: a shorthand here would sit after
37	  // paddingBlock above and reset it back to 0.
38	  paddingInline: 0,
39	  textDecoration: 'none',
40	  // Inner span carries the underline. Use transparent instead of 'none' so
41	  // border-color transitions smoothly on hover/active without a display change.
42	  '& > span': {
43	    borderBottom: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid transparent',
44	    transition: `border-color var(--zimm-motion-duration-fast) var(--zimm-motion-easing-standard)`,
45	  },
46	  _hover: {
47	    '& > span': { borderBottomColor: 'currentColor' },
48	  },
49	  // Active (aria-current="page"): permanent underline regardless of hover
50	  '&[aria-current="page"] > span': {
51	    borderBottomColor: 'currentColor',
52	  },
53	};
54	
55	const variants = {
56	  light: {
57	    color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
58	    _focusVisible: {
59	      outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
60	      outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
61	      boxShadow: 'none',
62	    },
63	  },

66	    _focusVisible: {
67	      outline: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-text-inverse)',
68	      outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
69	      boxShadow: 'none',
70	    },
71	  },
72	};
73	
74	export const ZimmNavItem = defineStyleConfig({
75	  baseStyle,
76	  variants,
77	  defaultProps: { variant: 'light' },
78	});
